requestKey: How do I plan outfits from my own wardrobe?|cherly.app|sample1

payload.text:
Here’s a simple, repeatable system to plan outfits from what you already own.

1) Set your constraints
- Look at your next 7–10 days: occasions, dress codes, and how much moving/commuting you’ll do.
- Pick a base palette you actually wear: 1–2 base neutrals (e.g., navy, black, tan), 1–2 accent colors, and any prints that include those colors.

2) Inventory quickly (30–45 minutes)
- Pull items into piles by category: tops, bottoms, layers, dresses/sets, shoes.
- Mark favorites you reach for and “orphans” you like but don’t wear. Note why (fit, no matching shoes, too dressy, etc.).
- Aim for each bottom to pair with at least 3 tops. If it can’t, it needs a partner piece or it’s a candidate to tailor/rehome.

3) Build mix-and-match clusters
- Create 1–3 small clusters you can wear many ways:
  - Cluster formula: 3 tops + 3 bottoms + 2 layers + 2 shoes in the same palette.
  - That yields 18+ outfits fast. Add 2–3 accessories (belt, scarf/hat, jewelry) to change the vibe.
- Outfit formulas to start with:
  - Column of color (matching top + bottom) + contrast layer.
  - Big-over-small or small-over-big (e.g., oversized top + slim bottom, or fitted top + wide-leg bottom).
  - Dress or matching set + third piece (blazer, cardigan, denim/leather jacket).
  - Tee/button-down + trousers/jeans + “third piece” + non-sneaker shoe for instant polish.

4) Plan your week
- Check your calendar and weather, then pre-select 5 looks from your clusters.
- Lay them out or hang them together with their shoes/accessories.
- Take quick mirror photos. Create an album called “Outfit Menu – Summer (or current season).”
- Add one backup outfit that works for most days.

5) Finishers that make outfits feel intentional
- Proportion: aim for the rule of thirds (top roughly 1/3, bottom 2/3, or vice versa). Front-tuck, roll sleeves, or cuff hems to adjust.
- Bookend colors: repeat a color at your shoes and near your face (glasses/earrings/lip, hat, scarf).
- Texture mix: pair matte with shiny, smooth with nubby (denim + silk, knit + leather) to avoid flat looks.

6) Troubleshoot and refine
- If an item is hard to style, try it three ways now. If it still fails, list why: needs tailoring? missing the right shoe/belt? Put those gaps on a “smart list” for future shopping.
- Note comfort issues (slips, rides up, too warm). Solve with underlayers, tailoring, or retire it.

7) Maintain by season
- Rotate off-season items to a bin; keep one small “wild card” section for statement pieces you love.
- Update your Outfit Menu with only the photos you actually wore and liked (rating 1–5 helps).

Quick start in 20 minutes today
- Choose one base color (e.g., navy).
- Pull: 2 bottoms in that color family, 3 tops that match both, 1 light layer, 1 dark layer, 2 shoes.
- Make 5 outfits, shoot quick photos, and schedule which day you’ll wear each.

Want personalized outfits from your actual wardrobe? Tell me:
- Your typical week (work/casual/dressy %), climate, and any dress code.
- Colors you love/avoid and the 10–15 pieces you wear most.
Or upload a few mirror pics/flat-lays of items, and I’ll build clusters and a week-long Outfit Menu for you.
